title: The doers of good still live in awe of their Lord.
subtitle: Good deeds paired with humble fear
then: After the warning about those who feel secure in their wealth, the surah describes the opposite. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: {idea}the believer combines excellence with awe{/idea}, {trap}while the disbeliever combines evil deeds with a sense of security{/trap}.
now: You prayed all five today, gave to the fundraiser, called your mother. A small voice says: I am one of the good ones now. {idea}The verse keeps that voice humble.{/idea}
old: Once I am doing good, I can stop worrying.
new: Doing good and staying in awe of Allah go together.
try: After your next good deed, say quietly: O Allah, accept it from me.

title: They believe in the signs of their Lord.
subtitle: Signs in creation and in revelation
then: Ibn Kathir says they believe in {idea}His universal and legislative signs{/idea}, as Maryam testified to {reward}the words of her Lord and His scriptures{/reward}. She accepted that what exists happens by His decree, and what He commands is what He loves.
now: You accept the verses that comfort you and scroll past the ones that ask something hard. You thank Allah for the good news and blame bad luck for the rest. {idea}Belief takes both.{/idea}
old: I believe in the parts that make sense to me.
new: Everything that happens and everything He commands are signs from the same Lord.
try: Read one verse today that you usually skip, and sit with what it asks of you.

title: They give their Lord no partners.
subtitle: Worship kept for Allah alone

row.title: Allah alone
sub: no wife, no offspring, no equal

then: Ibn Kathir says they {idea}worship Him alone and know there is no god but Allah, the One, the Self-Sufficient{/idea}, with none comparable or equal to Him. It comes right after awe and belief, as their foundation.
now: You would never bow to a statue. But the job, the approval of people, the money that you check five times a day. {trap}Partners can sneak in without a shrine.{/trap}
old: Shirk is something only idol-worshippers do.
new: Keeping Allah alone means watching what quietly takes His place in my heart.
try: Ask yourself honestly: what did I think about most today? Give that worry to Allah in dua.

title: They give, and still fear it may not be accepted.
subtitle: Generous hands, humble hearts
then: Aisha asked the Prophet ﷺ if these were people who sin while fearing Allah. He said: {idea}no, daughter of As-Siddiq, they are those who pray, fast and give in charity, fearing it will not be accepted from them.{/idea}
now: You hit donate and a little pride rises: that was generous. {idea}This verse describes a different feeling: hoping it is enough, not sure, still giving.{/idea}
old: Once I have given, my part is done and counted.
new: I give my best and still hope Allah accepts it.
try: Give something small today in secret, then ask Allah to accept it.

title: These are the ones racing to good deeds.
subtitle: The real hastening to good
then: Verse 56 asked whether wealth meant Allah was {trap}hastening good things{/trap} to the heedless. Here the same word turns: the people of awe, belief, and humble giving are {idea}the ones who hasten to good deeds and are foremost in them.{/idea}
now: Someone in the family chat asks for help and you wait to see if anyone else answers first. {idea}The verse describes the one who answers first, without waiting.{/idea}
old: Someone else will step up for that.
new: Being first to do good is the race worth winning.
try: When the next request for help comes today, be the first to respond.

title: No soul is asked beyond what it can carry.
subtitle: Fair burden, a truthful record

row.title: I can never be like them

then: After describing the foremost in good, Allah reassures: {idea}He does not burden any soul with more than it can bear.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says the record omits {reward}none of their good deeds{/reward}, and for His believing servants He will {reward}forgive and overlook many evil ones{/reward}.
now: You read about people who pray all night and give half their salary, and you feel tired just hearing it. You are a parent with a newborn, or working two jobs. {idea}He asks what you can carry, and records every bit of it.{/idea}
old: If I cannot do it all, it is not worth trying.
new: Allah asks within my capacity, and not one good deed is lost.
try: Pick one good deed that truly fits your life right now, and do it today without guilt.

title: Their hearts are covered over, busy with other deeds.
subtitle: Heedlessness that fills the day
then: Ibn Kathir says their hearts were {trap}covered because of negligence and misguidance{/trap} from the Quran, and they had {trap}other deeds they kept doing{/trap}. Ibn Abbas said this meant the evil they were set on.
now: The Quran sits on the shelf in the living room, a little dusty. The TV is on, the phone is on, the to-do list is long. {trap}It is not that you hate it. You are just covered over.{/trap}
old: I would read more Quran if I had time.
new: A heart can get so covered with busyness that it stops hearing.
try: Put the Quran somewhere you will see it first thing tomorrow, and read one page.

title: When punishment seizes the comfortable, they cry out.
subtitle: Loud calls that come too late
then: Ibn Kathir says when Allah's punishment overtakes {trap}those living a happy life of luxury{/trap}, they {trap}scream their calls for help{/trap}. He cites another verse: they cried out {trap}when there was no longer time for escape.{/trap}
now: Some people only remember to pray in the hospital waiting room. {idea}Calling on Allah in a crisis is good. Knowing Him before the crisis is better.{/idea}
old: I will turn to Allah when I really need Him.
new: The time to call on Allah is now, while things are easy.
try: Make one dua of thanks today on an ordinary, easy day.

title: Do not cry out today; no help is coming.
subtitle: A door that closes
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}no one is going to save you from what has happened, whether you scream or stay silent. There is no escape.{/trap} It is a sober picture of a moment when crying out is too late.
now: Right now, today, your dua is heard. Your tawbah is accepted. {reward}The door this verse describes as closed is wide open for you.{/reward} That is the point of hearing it now.
new: Repentance is open now, and that is a mercy I should not waste.
try: Make sincere tawbah tonight for one specific thing.

title: The verses were read to you, and you turned on your heels.
subtitle: The greatest of their sins
then: Ibn Kathir says this is the {trap}greatest of their sins{/trap}: the verses were recited to them, and {trap}when they were called, they refused and resisted{/trap}. They were not ignorant. They walked away.
now: The khutbah touches exactly your problem and you think, that is for other people. A friend shares a verse and you swipe past. {trap}Turning on your heels can look like a thumb flicking upward.{/trap}
new: Hearing it and turning away is worse than never hearing it.
try: When a verse lands on you today, stop scrolling and read it twice.

title: Proud of the House, they spent nights talking against it.
subtitle: Late-night talk and empty pride
then: Ibn Abbas said the Quraysh {trap}boasted about the Kabah: we are its people who stay up talking at night.{/trap} They did not use it for its purpose, {trap}so in effect they had abandoned it{/trap}. He said late-night chatter became disliked after this verse.
now: You live near the masjid, or come from a religious family, and that feels like a credential. Meanwhile midnight is for the group chat, the gossip, the scrolling. {idea}Being close to something holy is not the same as living by it.{/idea}
old: My background and closeness to religion protect me.
new: Closeness means nothing if I do not live by what I am close to.
try: Close the chats an hour earlier tonight and spend five minutes in dua or Quran.

title: Have they not reflected on the Quran?
subtitle: A gift given to them, unread
then: Ibn Kathir says no Book or warner had come to their forefathers, so they should have {reward}accepted it, given thanks, tried to understand it and acted on it night and day{/reward}. Qatadah said if they had pondered it, {idea}they would have found a deterrent from disobeying Allah{/idea}.
now: You can recite Al-Fatiha in your sleep, but if someone asked what verse five means, you would pause. {idea}The verse is not asking whether you have heard it. It asks whether you have thought about it.{/idea}
old: I know the Quran because I have read it.
new: Knowing the Quran begins when I stop and think about what it says.
try: Pick one short verse you recite daily. Read its meaning today and think about it for two minutes.

title: Did they not know their own Messenger?
subtitle: They knew his honesty since childhood
then: Ibn Kathir asks: {idea}do they not recognize the honesty, trustworthiness and good character with which he grew up among them?{/idea} Even Abu Sufyan, before Islam, when asked by Heraclius, {reward}could only admit he was noble and truthful{/reward}.
now: You know the person who always tells you the truth, even when it is uncomfortable. When they warn you, you still look for reasons to doubt. {idea}Their track record is the evidence.{/idea}
old: I need to judge every claim from scratch.
new: A lifetime of honesty is strong evidence, and I should honor it.
try: Thank someone today whose honesty you have always been able to rely on.

title: He brought the truth, and most of them disliked it.
subtitle: The problem was not madness but aversion
then: Ibn Kathir says the Quraysh {trap}called him mad or said he made it up, but their hearts did not believe that{/trap}. They knew. Allah names the real reason: {trap}most of them are averse to the truth.{/trap}
now: The doctor says cut the sugar. The friend says you were rude. The verse says pray. {trap}Sometimes you call the message unclear because you do not like what it asks.{/trap}
old: I reject this because it does not make sense.
new: Sometimes I reject a truth because I dislike it, not because it is wrong.
try: Name one truth you have been resisting. Admit to yourself that you know it is true.
